content.comment_body: Good morning. How can we transfer a locked program using a memory card to the [product_name] hardware? (such as a red memory card) Thanks.

You need to save the [product_name] program as a binary dump to your computer. Go to File > Save as > Binary dump (*.bin). The software restricts the file name, so you will save it as "[product_name]_U_P.bin". After saving, copy it from your computer to the microSD card. Switch off the power for the [product_name], insert the microSD card, and switch power back on. Upon restart, the device loads the program from the microSD card and stores it in its program memory.
What do you mean by 'red memory card'? Are you referring to the memory cards from older [product_name] versions (for example, [article_no])? If so, unfortunately there is no possibility.

Thank you. My issue persists. The current method does not offer proper security. The [product_name] now operates without the card, allowing the client to copy the program to many units. My aim is for the program to only work with the memory card, preventing any copying.
No, I only want to send a program with a memory card. The program is locked and was done as you described. Thank you.
What confused me was the term 'red memory card' because in [product_name] [article_no] there is no 'red memory card', but rather just a microSD card.

My issue persists. This solution does not provide security. The [product_name] operates without the card, so the client is able to duplicate the program across multiple devices. My objective is for the program to function only with the memory card, preventing any unauthorized copying. Thanks.

Unfortunately, that's not possible. After a restart, the [product_name] copies the program from the microSD card to its internal memory. The microSD card can then be removed, and the program remains in internal memory until deleted or replaced. There is no function to force the device to work only when the program remains on the microSD card.
Okay, thank you once again. Thanks in several languages.
Even if this function existed in the [product_name], your customer could still copy the microSD card multiple times.
The only conclusion is direct programming on the device, locking both the program and the hardware.
That's correct. Program directly on the [product_name] device and switch it into operator mode.
Hello, a [product_name] with a microSD card does include some copy protection, similar to older versions. Refer to chapter 11.2.2 in the device manual. Hope this assists.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is trying to protect their proprietary logic for the [product_name] hardware by using memory card distribution, wanting to prevent unauthorized duplication or execution on other devices. Clarifications were made about how locked programs can be transferred. However, the current [product_name] lacks the enforcement mechanism to ensure the program operates only when the original memory card is present. As a result, the protection measures do not meet the user's needs, leading to frustration because clients can freely copy the program.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the system to allow running the program only when the original memory card is inserted, thus preventing program copying and unauthorized use. They are seeking stronger protection and access restrictions for their intellectual property on the device.
